`clever drain` now takes a `--type <type>` option and lists only the drains of that recipient type. I haven't run it against a real account yet, so the filtering itself is untested.

**What changed** (`src/commands/drain/drain.command.js`):
- **Accepted values:** the same names the `drain create` subcommands use (`betterstack`, `datadog`, `elasticsearch`, `newrelic`, `ovh-tcp`, `raw-http`, `splunk`, `syslog-tcp`, `syslog-udp`), taken from `DRAIN_TYPES`. Any other value is rejected with the list of valid ones.
- **Where it applies:** the CLI fetches all drains, then keeps those whose recipient type matches. The filter applies to the table, the single-drain view and `--format json`.
- **No match:** the empty message names the type, for example "There are no Datadog drains for my-app".
- **Placement:** since only this command uses the option, it's defined in the command file, like `--source-token` in `drain create betterstack`.

The regenerated `drain.docs.md` and `skills/clever-tools/references/full-documentation.md` are included.

**Checks:**
- Lint, typecheck, docs check and unit tests (23/23) pass, and `drain --help` shows the option.
- `npm run validate` as a whole fails at the format check, on `.claude/settings.json` only. I didn't touch that file, and prettier passes on `src`, `docs` and `skills`.
- `node_modules` was missing, so I ran `npm ci` to generate the docs.

**Still to do:**
- **Test on an account:** `node bin/clever.js drain --app <app> --type datadog` is read-only. I didn't run it because the task didn't name an app.
- **User guide:** you declined my edit to `docs/services-logs-drains.md`, which added `clever drain --type <DRAIN-TYPE>` to its list of commands. The project rules say to keep that guide up to date, so you may want to add the line yourself, or let me.

Nothing is committed. When you do commit, `feat(drain): ...` fits the project's conventions, and the PR needs a `Closes #N` issue.
